newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas still down late on cash, charts.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas still down late on cash, charts.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained broadly lower late Friday in moderate trade, hit by reports of crumbling cash prices and technical selling after March broke trendline support early, industry sources said.
At 1430 EST, March tumbled 14.1 cents to $2.22 per million British thermal units, while April was 6.3 cents lower at $2.115. Most others were off by 1.3 to 3.5 cents.

"Some people are hoping this (the selloff) is just a weekend phenomenon, but that may be just hope. The screen looks pretty weak," said one Texas trader, adding cash prices may stay on the defensive with no extreme cold ahead.

While some forecasters were looking for some slightly below-normal Midwest and Northeast weather next week, traders said it was not likely to be cold enough to balance the market, particularly with eastern storage operators and utilities looking to trim a rising stock surplus before winter draws to a close next month.

And technical traders also were bearish after March's break today of trendline support in the low-$2.30s. Most expect the spot contract to soon test next support at the Nov 5 low of $2.12. March resistance was seen in the low-$2.50s and then in the $2.70 and $2.80 area.

In the cash, weekend Gulf Coast prices skidded 10-15 cents Friday to the mid-$2.30s. Midcon pipes were off about a nickel to the $2.30-35 area. New York city gate gas was quoted more than 10 cents lower at about $2.90.
NYMEX said 21,771 Hub contracts traded by 1405 EST. NYMEX Hub open interest on Feb 6 rose 329 contracts to 159,920.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas were untraded at 1430 EST.
On the KCBT, March fell 11.9 cents to $1.98, while deferreds were down by one to 6.3 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 2.2 cents to 24 cents (NYMEX premium).
